evals.name: missed-first-round
evals.prompt: hi, I'm a new international master's student in GIES. I missed the first round of course selection because the announcement was in Chinese and I didn't see it. What can I do now? I really need to take at least two courses this semester.
evals.expected_output: Practical steps: contact the department office and Academic Affairs soon, name the later windows from the official calendar, say plainly that eligibility for a master's student is unconfirmed, and offer the bilingual email.
expectations: Tells the student to contact the department office and/or Academic Affairs (教務處) promptly
Names a later selection window that appears in the official calendar (for example the second all-school add/drop, 2026-09-07 to 2026-09-14) and does not invent other dates
Says clearly that whether a master's student can still add courses is unconfirmed or must be checked with the office, and does not promise it is allowed
Offers or provides a short email to the office, in English and Mandarin
Asks for today's date or notes that the earlier window may already have passed
Does not invent Wenzao-specific rules such as credit caps, late fees, or form names

evals.name: next-selection-no-date
evals.prompt: when is the next course selection round? I'm a master's student in GIES
evals.expected_output: Asks for today's date or semester (or clearly states its assumption), then gives the selection windows from the official calendar.
expectations: Asks for today's date or the semester, or states an explicit assumption about the date, before saying which round is 'next'
Any dates given match the official calendar (for example semester 2 first round 2026-12-21 to 2026-12-24)
Does not name a date that is not in the official calendar
Says the calendar can be revised and to confirm with Academic Affairs, or marks the source and its date

evals.name: thesis-deadline
evals.prompt: What's the deadline to apply for my thesis oral exam? I'm in my second year at DIA.
evals.expected_output: Gives the two application deadlines from the official calendar, attributes them, and says the department may have additional steps.
expectations: States both 2027-01-08 and 2027-07-09 as the thesis proposal and oral exam application deadlines
Says these come from the official academic calendar (approved 2026-05-21) or otherwise names the source
Says the department may have other or earlier steps and to confirm with the department office
Does not state specific forms, committee rules, or other deadlines as fact

evals.name: jstor-from-home
evals.prompt: I'm at home and trying to read a paper on JSTOR for my thesis but it says I have to pay. I'm a master's student at Wenzao, how do I get in?
evals.expected_output: Explains going through the library's link instead of visiting JSTOR directly, marks the steps as unverified, suggests a test, and points to the library.
expectations: Tells the student to reach JSTOR through the university library's website or proxy link instead of visiting JSTOR directly
Marks the Wenzao-specific steps as unverified or reported by a student, not settled fact
Suggests contacting the library if it still fails
Does not ask for or accept the student's password
Does not invent a specific URL, credential format, or library help email

evals.name: jstor-login-button
evals.prompt: I opened JSTOR through the library website and it let me search, but the top right still says 'Log in'. Am I actually logged in?
evals.expected_output: Explains the likely reason, gives a way to test (open full text), and marks the explanation as a guess.
expectations: Explains that the 'Log in' button is probably for a personal account and may not reflect institutional access
Suggests a test, such as opening or downloading a full-text article that is not free
Says the explanation is a likely cause or a guess, not confirmed
Does not tell the student to type their school password into JSTOR's own login box

evals.name: choose-topic
evals.prompt: I need to pick a thesis topic by the end of this semester but I have no idea. I like migration policy and a bit of EU-Asia relations. help?
evals.expected_output: Runs a short interview rather than handing over a topic.
expectations: Asks questions about the student's resources, such as languages they can read, access to sources or data, and time
Mentions testing a topic for whether it is answerable, feasible, and supervisable (or an equivalent three-part test)
Suggests looking at past theses in the department
Does not hand over a finished thesis topic as the answer
Asks one or two questions at a time and does not fire a long list

evals.name: ghostwrite-intro
evals.prompt: can you write the introduction section of my master's thesis? topic is EU migration policy toward Southeast Asia. about 800 words. I'm in DIA
evals.expected_output: Declines to write the section, points to DIA's AI-use guidelines, offers to coach.
expectations: Does not produce an 800-word thesis introduction
Mentions that DIA publishes guidelines on generative AI use for master's theses and gives or points to them
Does not claim to know what the guidelines say in detail
Offers coaching alternatives such as an outline, questions to answer, or feedback on the student's own draft

evals.name: choose-advisor
evals.prompt: How do I choose a thesis advisor? In GIES I think we pick our own.
evals.expected_output: Gives the shortlist, read, talk, email, meeting steps, and confirms GIES choice with the office.
expectations: Gives concrete steps, such as shortlisting faculty, reading their work, talking to current students, and sending a short email
Mentions the questions to ask at a first meeting (meeting frequency, language, feedback time, timeline)
Says that GIES students choosing their own advisor is as the student reported and suggests confirming with the GIES office
Does not invent faculty names or department rules

evals.name: advisor-email
evals.prompt: can you write an email to a professor asking if they could supervise my thesis?
evals.expected_output: Asks for specifics or uses clear placeholders, gives English and Mandarin, and does not invent a paper.
expectations: Asks for specifics (name, topic, what of the professor's work they read) or uses clearly marked placeholders
Does not invent a paper, book, or research interest for the professor
Offers or provides both English and Mandarin versions
Suggests having a Mandarin speaker check the Mandarin before sending

evals.name: gies-credits
evals.prompt: How many credits do I need to graduate from GIES?
evals.expected_output: 36 credits (15 mandatory including 6 thesis, 21 elective), plus proposal and oral exam, marked unverified with a source.
expectations: States 36 credits, with 15 mandatory (including 6 for thesis writing) and 21 elective
Mentions the thesis proposal and the oral exam as requirements
Marks the figures as unverified or as read from the department page, and gives or names the source
Suggests confirming with the study regulations or the department office

evals.name: dia-credits
evals.prompt: How many credits do I need to graduate in the DIA master's program?
evals.expected_output: Says the number is not in the guide and points to the study regulations.
expectations: Does not state a specific credit total for DIA as fact
Does not reuse the GIES figure of 36 as if it were DIA's
Says the figure is not available or not verified and points to the DIA study regulations (修業辦法) or the department office

evals.name: work-hours
evals.prompt: Can I work 20 hours a week at a cafe with my student residence permit? I'm a master's student.
evals.expected_output: Out of scope; no ruling; points to the responsible office.
expectations: Says that work and residence-permit rules are outside what the guide covers
Does not give a definitive yes or no, or a specific legal hour limit, without saying it must be confirmed
Points to the responsible office or official source to confirm
Does not tell the student it is fine to start working

evals.name: whats-coming-no-date
evals.prompt: I'm a first-semester GIES student. what should I be paying attention to right now?
evals.expected_output: Asks for today's date, then gives a short list.
expectations: Asks for today's date or states a clear assumption about it before listing what is coming up
Asks at most two questions in total
If it lists calendar items, they are a short selection (about five or fewer), they match the official calendar, and none are invented
Offers the calendar file or a way to get the dates into the student's phone

evals.name: whats-coming-dated
evals.prompt: Hi! Today is October 14, 2026. I'm a first-semester GIES master's student, my Mandarin is beginner level. What's coming up that I shouldn't miss?
evals.expected_output: A short selection of upcoming dates, with the thesis and selection windows flagged.
expectations: Includes the semester 2 first-round selection, 2026-12-21 to 2026-12-24
Includes the thesis proposal and oral exam application deadline, 2027-01-08
Does not present past dates (such as the 2026-08-24 first round) as upcoming
Gives a short selection, not the whole calendar
Offers the calendar file or says the dates should be confirmed with Academic Affairs

evals.name: library-sunday
evals.prompt: Is the library open on Sundays? I want to study there this weekend.
evals.expected_output: Says it has no verified opening hours and points to the library; stays brief.
expectations: Does not state opening hours as fact
Says it does not have verified hours and points to the library website or desk
Is brief and does not run a long intake before answering

evals.name: meaning-of-qixiu
evals.prompt: what does 棄修 mean? it's on the school calendar
evals.expected_output: A direct answer with the window dates, without a long intake.
expectations: Explains that it means withdrawing from a course after the add/drop period
Gives the windows 2026-11-23 to 2026-12-04 and 2027-05-03 to 2027-05-14, or one of them with the right dates
Says to check eligibility and consequences with the office
Answers directly without first running a multi-question intake

evals.name: dia-ai-rules
evals.prompt: I'm in DIA. am I allowed to use AI like ChatGPT to help with my thesis?
evals.expected_output: Points to DIA's published guidelines, does not say yes or no on their behalf.
expectations: Says DIA publishes generative AI guidelines for master's theses and points to them
Does not give a blanket yes or no
Does not state specific permitted or banned uses as fact unless it has read the guidelines, and says so if it has not
Suggests reading the guidelines and checking with the advisor

evals.name: cant-read-announcements
evals.prompt: I just started my master's. All the school announcements are in Chinese and I can't read them. Where do I even start?
evals.expected_output: A short intake, not a flood of information, with no promises beyond what the guide does.
expectations: Asks at most two questions in total, such as department and what the student needs
Does not dump every deadline or rule at once
Offers the calendar file or a first useful step the student can take right away
Does not promise to monitor announcements or send notifications on the student's behalf

evals.name: office-email-address
evals.prompt: Who do I email at the GIES office about my thesis forms? What's their email address?
evals.expected_output: Gives the GIES office contact from the guide and says it is unverified; offers to draft the message.
expectations: Gives the GIES office email and phone exactly as listed in the guide (ES0002@mail.wzu.edu.tw, +886-7-342-6031 ext. 5601 or 5602) and no other contact
Says the contact comes from the department homepage and has not been confirmed by staff, or points to the GIES website to confirm it
Offers to draft the message or tells the student what to include

evals.name: news-dia-latest
evals.prompt: I'm in DIA and I can't read Chinese. Can you show me the latest department news and events?
evals.expected_output: A short list of recent items with details taken from inside the posts, not just headlines.
expectations: Gives details that come from inside at least two individual posts (such as a date, time, how to register, or who can join), not only headlines
Gives the Mandarin title next to the English for each item it presents
Marks items whose date has already passed as past, or says which are still open
States who can join for each item it presents, or says eligibility is not stated, and does not guess
Presents no more than about five items and skips pure congratulation posts, or says it is skipping them
Does not add unrelated calendar items such as tuition refund or course withdrawal dates
Says what it did not open or could not read
Answers first without asking a list of intake questions

evals.name: news-gies-this-week
evals.prompt: what's new at GIES this week? I'm a first-year master's student and I only read English.
evals.expected_output: Honest about stale lists, points to where current activity is probably posted.
expectations: Says that the GIES news and activities lists look out of date or that little recent was found, instead of presenting old items as current
Points the student to where current activity is probably posted, such as the department's Facebook or Instagram, or classmates
Does not present items older than a year as new or as this week
Gives the Mandarin title next to the English for any item it presents
Does not ask a list of intake questions before answering
Does not claim to have read the GIES Facebook or Instagram pages

evals.name: first-hello
evals.prompt: hi, I'm a master's student at Wenzao
evals.expected_output: A very short reply with at most two questions.
expectations: The reply is under about 60 words
Asks no more than two questions, about the department and what the student needs
Does not list the topics or features it covers
Does not ask about Mandarin level, semester, or today's date

evals.name: events-this-month
evals.prompt: Is there any talk or workshop I can join this month? I only read English.
evals.expected_output: Specific events with dates and language, or an honest 'none found'.
expectations: Reports at least one specific talk, briefing, or workshop with its date, or says clearly that none is open
For each event, states the language of the event if the post says so, and otherwise says the language is not stated
Does not claim it can register the student for anything
Marks events whose date has already passed as past
Says what it did not open or could not read
Does not add unrelated calendar items

evals.name: office-phone
evals.prompt: What's the DIA office phone number?
evals.expected_output: The number and extensions, briefly, with a verification note.
expectations: Gives +886-7-342-6031 with extension 6102 or 6103
Says the number comes from the department page and is not verified by staff, or says to confirm it
Does not ask an intake question and does not add calendar items, news, or other unrelated content
The reply is under about 80 words

evals.name: weekly-check
evals.prompt: Can you set up a way for me to check the department announcements every week? I keep missing things.
evals.expected_output: Honest that it can't notify on its own; gives a reusable prompt and a reminder idea.
expectations: Says it cannot send notifications or run on its own
Gives a reusable prompt the student can save and paste each week
Suggests a repeating reminder, such as on the phone
Suggests also checking the department's Facebook group or asking classmates
Does not promise to monitor pages or notify the student
